To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MEM applied to a set of phased structure factors (F) from Rietvield refinement and a set of structure-factor amputudes (G) from Le Bail fits, in combination with charge flipping, is a powerful method to reveal the true nature of disorder from in situ powder diffraction data.
the combination of MEM with pCF is a powerful method to visualize the true disorder in disordered crystal structures.

the MEM is able to visualize the 'true' disorder of a crystal structure from powder diffraction data and that this is best done by applying the MEM to the combination of phases from charge flipping with the structure-factor ampli- tudes from Rietvield refinement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic evaluation of the ability of the MEM to reveal the ;true' structure of disordered crystals.
a new combination of MEM and pCF for electron density determination of highly disordered materials from X-ray powder data.
a powerful combination of the MEM and pCF, which is able to reveal the true nature of apparent structural disorder in in situ X-ray diffraction data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of MEM with charge flipping is a powerful tool to obtain the true structure of highly disordered materials, whereas the MEM applied to phased structure factors is a powerful tool for a detailed analysis of the structure of disordered materials.
the combination of the MEM and the pCF algorithm is a powerful tool to visualize the true disorder of crystal structures.

the combination of MEM and pCF provides a powerful and fast method of obtaining the most probable electron-density distribution in disordered materials, but that Rietveld methods, in particular those based on structure-factor ampltitudes, remain superior in terms of precision and reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MEM, in combination with a suitable set of constraints, can reconstruct the electron density in disordered structures with high precision, but that the MEM alone is not able to distinguish between different models of disorder.

MEM is a powerful tool for the visualization of the true nature of the crystal structures of disorded materials, and pCF is a powerful tool to obtain the phases needed to apply MEM to powder diffraction data in an ab initio way.
the MEM is a powerful tool to visualize structural disorder, provided that the correct phases of the structure factors are known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MEM can be used as a tool to visualize the true structure of disordered materials from powder data.
the MEM can be successfully applied to disordered crystal structures.
